question: A solid metallic toy has a hemispherical base with radius 3.5 cm surmounted by a cone. If the height of the cone is the same as the radius of its base, then the volume of metal used in cm³ is: ( Take pi ={22over7})
solution:
**Given**

Radius of hemisphere = 3.5 cm

Height of cone = Radius of cone

Radius of cone = 3.5 cm

**Formula used**

Volume of hemisphere = (2/3)πr3 

Volume of cone = (1/3)πr2h

where r and h are radius and height respectively

**Calculation**

The volume of metallic toy = Volume of hemisphere + volume of the cone

⇒ (2/3)πr³ + (1/3)πrR²h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a33ee2fe9450f5cc822ca5026766d076aed082b6e953ab5c9e521f5f608b1cbf.png] 

⇒ (2/3)πr3 + (1/3)πR²× R (As h = r)

⇒ (2/3)πr3 + (1/3)πR³

⇒ (3/3)πr3 (Since radius of hemisphere = radius of cone, so, R = r)

⇒ (22/7) × 3.5 × 3.5 × 3.5

⇒ 22 × 0.5 × 3.5 × 3.5

⇒ 11 × 12.25

⇒ 134.75

⇒ 134 + (75/100)

⇒ 1343over4cm³ 

**∴ The volume of metal used in a toy is 1343over4 cm³**
